Why: Decides which guardrails apply and right-sizes cost — don't over- or under-build.
Evidence: Tier + written rationale in the ServiceNow readiness record and an ADR.

Why: NFRs drive design and cost and are the thing most often missed.
Evidence: Completed NFR worksheet in the repo.

Why: Decisions must be traceable, not just diagrammed.
Evidence: /adr folder + diagram in the repo.

Item: Threat model + STRA (and PIA if personal information)
Why: Security & privacy risk must be assessed before build, not at go-live.
Evidence: STRA (+PIA) reference and status.

Why: Support needs the whole solution; old-vs-new must be traceable; dependencies visible.
Evidence: Living solution doc + changelog + integrations. In-house = Must; COTS = link the vendor's changelog.
Covers: Solution doc · changelog / release notes · integrations & dependencies

Why: Legally required for public-facing services (Accessible BC Act); expected internally.
Evidence: Accessibility conformance assessment against WCAG 2.2 AA.

Why: Funding must be secured before the project starts; no funded support = no go-live.
Evidence: Operating-cost estimate + Expense Authority approval + funded support model.
Covers: Cost estimate · EA approval · funded support model

Item: Use the standard CI/CD pipeline (BC Gov Quick Start template)
Why: One compliant pipeline bakes in everything below — don't reinvent it as 14 separate items.
Evidence: Repo on the Quick Start template, or GitHub Actions containing these stages.
Covers: Build · unit/integration tests · SAST · SCA · secret scan · image scan · SBOM · signing · provenance · DAST · licence check · dependency currency · signed commits · branch protection

Why: Coverage decays without a gate; contract tests protect integrations.
Evidence: Coverage gate — in-house 85% (T1/T2); COTS/contracted = report only.
Covers: Coverage gate · unit / integration / contract tests · UAT · test data

Item: Externalise configuration & secrets; deploy via IaC / GitOps
Why: Config in images or changed by hand causes drift; secrets never belong in code.
Evidence: Config per environment + managed secrets store ({{SECRETS}}) + IaC in the repo.
Covers: Externalised config · managed secrets · IaC · GitOps

Why: Salesforce enforces hard per-transaction limits and deploys metadata, not containers.
Evidence: Bulkified code + documented sandbox & deployment path.
Covers: Governor limits / bulkification · sandbox & deployment strategy

Why: Infrastructure is only ~half of resilience — the application itself must be built for it.
Evidence: Conformance to the BC Gov app-resiliency guidelines / 12-factor.
Covers: Stateless · timeouts & retries with backoff · idempotency · circuit breakers · graceful shutdown · health probes · >=2 replicas / PDB · resource limits / HPA · zero-downtime + progressive delivery

Why: Peak load and failure are where apps fall over — prove it before users do.
Evidence: Load/performance test to peak + chaos/failover test + capacity/autoscaling validation.
Covers: Load / peak test · chaos / failover test · capacity & autoscaling validation

Why: Someone must own quality, definitions and access; classification drives controls.
Evidence: Classification + named Data Owner/Steward/Custodian + Data Interoperability engaged.
Covers: Data classification · Owner / Steward / Custodian · Data Interoperability

Why: Data can't grow forever; retention is legal / FOIPPA-driven.
Evidence: Retention/archival/deletion schedule implemented in the app.

Why: An untested backup is not a backup; you only know your RTO once you've failed over.
Evidence: HA data layer + tested restore (meets RPO) + DR/failover tested (Tier 1).
Covers: HA data layer · tested restore (RPO) · DR / failover (RTO)

Why: You can't operate what you can't see.
Evidence: Metrics + dashboards ({{MONITOR}}) + structured logs with trace IDs ({{LOGS}}) + tracing.
Covers: Metrics & dashboards · structured logs · distributed tracing

Why: Alerts with no SLO or owner are just noise.
Evidence: SLIs/SLOs defined + actionable alerts routed to the on-call owner.

Why: Use approved SSO; least-privilege RBAC; a defined access process.
Evidence: IDIR/Keycloak/BC Services Card + RBAC + access-management process (approvers/support).
Covers: SSO (IDIR / Keycloak / BCSC) · RBAC · access-management process

Why: Govern endpoints centrally: auth, rate limiting/throttling, and versioning.
Evidence: APS (gov API gateway) config; versioned, backward-compatible API.
Covers: API gateway (APS) · rate limiting / throttling · versioning & backward compatibility

Why: Encrypt data, keep it in an approved region, and design for privacy (FOIPPA).
Evidence: TLS in transit + at-rest encryption + data residency + privacy-by-design notes.
Covers: Encryption in transit & at rest · data residency (in-Canada) · privacy-by-design

Why: Independent testing catches what the pipeline misses; findings need a fix-by clock.
Evidence: Penetration test (orderable service) + TLS scan + owned vulnerability-management SLAs.
Covers: Penetration test · TLS scan · vulnerability-management SLAs

Why: Someone who didn't build it must be able to operate it, and support must be funded.
Evidence: Runbook (deploy/rollback/restart/failures/escalation) + agreed on-call/support hours.

Why: The CMDB is where apps are tracked; change needs control and a rollback authority.
Evidence: CMDB CI + change/release process + named rollback authority.
Covers: CMDB registration · change / release management · rollback authority

Why: The front line takes the calls; defects and training must transfer.
Evidence: Service Desk enabled (script/KB/escalation) + defect tombstone list + user docs/training.
Covers: Service Desk · defect tombstone list · user docs & training

Why: Apps without a retirement plan become zombie risk (orphaned data, expiring certs).
Evidence: Decommission plan: data disposition, teardown steps, named owner.

Why: If it isn't in the contract, the vendor isn't obliged to do it.
Evidence: SOW listing coverage %, SBOM, runbook, support terms, SLA, third-party support agreements, maintenance terms.
Covers: Coverage % · SBOM · runbook · support terms · SLA · third-party support · maintenance terms
